checks: If x-y belongs to 2L then their midpoint belongs to c+L and to conv(P), so completeness gives an atom in P. The general parent needs only membership of that midpoint, without imposing any condition on its label. The positive finite weight law and intrinsic closed halfspace traces match exactly.

At the simultaneously chosen strict-face center, the comparison gives E_p>=T_p>=D_p>=M/k. If E_p>T_p it is immediately strictly above M/k. If E_p=T_p, the exact pointwise criterion gives E_p=M_p, which is strictly above M/k by the same center’s face-mass property. This establishes strictness outside the exception without asserting the halfspace depth itself is strict.

In the exception each p is a vertex with a singleton minimal face, so every E_p=m_p=M/k. The same-coset midpoint condition also means distinct vertices cannot repeat a label when every point of P is a vertex. Rank zero has a singleton P, k=1 and value M. The finite positive support ensures the stated maximum exists.

Because L/2L has size 2 to the lattice rank, M/k>=M/2^n when rank L<=n. Since M>0, equality in the ambient bound forces k=2^n and equality in the occupied-count bound; both conditions are sufficient. The cube conv({0,1}^n) intersects the integer lattice precisely in those binary vertices, which occupy distinct cosets. Equal vertex masses therefore attain both bounds.

For the incomplete support the integer determinants of the cyclic pairs of edge vectors are 2,4,4,2,4. The signed determinants relative to each oriented edge are zero on its two endpoints and strictly positive on the other three points; this verifies all five listed supporting lines and strict vertex status. All five singleton energies are 1, while M/4=5/4, and the omitted point (1,0) is the midpoint of the first edge. The occupied count is also k=2, so the same example violates the occupied-count lower bound if completeness is removed.
